name: Grossmünster
overview: The Grossmünster is a Romanesque-style Protestant church and one of Zurich's most recognized landmarks. Its twin towers dominate the city skyline and offer spectacular panoramic views of Zurich and Lake Zurich.
history: According to legend, Charlemagne founded the Grossmünster after his horse fell to its knees over the grave of Zurich's patron saints Felix and Regula. Construction began around 1100, and it became the center of the Swiss Reformation under Huldrych Zwingli in the 16th century.
highlights: Modern stained glass windows by Augusto Giacometti
tips: Climb the 187 steps to Karlsturm tower for best views. Entry to church is free, tower climb has small fee. Best visited in late afternoon for golden hour photography. Audio guides available.
